title: The Great American Crossing — Chicago to San Francisco by Rail
pill: ★ THE GREAT AMERICAN CROSSING · COAST TO COAST BY RAIL
sub: Chicago to San Francisco on the storied Zephyr route — the plains, the Rockies' canyons, the desert and the Sierra, from the dome car and the dining car. Tap a leg to ride it.
cap: Modelled on the real California Zephyr route — real stations, canyons and passes shown accurately with facts from public sources. The operator and package are a generic composite (SO-1b) — a demo a real rail-tour operator could publish. Prices indicative (±) — booking, availability and seats are the agency's craft. Photos pending — AI imagery joins later.
route_summary: Whole route · 5 legs · ~3,900 km · 2 nights aboard + 2 stopover nights. True price: the real Zephyr runs coach from ±US$150, roomette from ±US$1,100 pp; escorted luxury rail from ±US$6,000. This composite journey: ±US$6,900 pp all-in — fares indicative, confirm with agency.

days.title: Chicago to the Mississippi and the plains
days.summary: Out of Chicago's great hall and west across Illinois — the Mississippi crossing at sunset, then the long prairie night to Omaha and the Nebraska dawn.

stops.name: Chicago Union Station — boarding
stops.blurb: Beneath the Great Hall's skylight the great western trains still depart — your sleeper waits on the lower level.

stops.name: The Mississippi crossing
stops.blurb: The train slows onto the high bridge at Burlington — America's river wide and slow beneath the dining car.

stops.name: Roomette night — the prairie run
stops.blurb: Your first night in the roomette: beds made down while you dine, Nebraska rolling past in the dark.

days.title: Denver and the Front Range climb
days.summary: Denver at breakfast, then the astonishing climb — thirty tunnels up the Front Range to the Moffat Tunnel under the Continental Divide.

stops.name: Breakfast into Denver Union
stops.blurb: Eggs and coffee as the Rockies fill the horizon — Denver's restored Union Station gleams beneath the mountains.

stops.name: The Front Range tunnels
stops.blurb: The train coils up the wall of the Rockies through thirty tunnels — flatland to alpine in an hour, finishing under the Divide itself.

stops.name: Winter Park & the high parks
stops.blurb: Out of the Moffat Tunnel into a bowl of ski country and high meadow — the roof of the route.

days.title: The canyons to Glenwood Springs
days.summary: The afternoon every rail lover rides for — three canyons of the Colorado River seen only from the train, then a hot-springs evening at Glenwood.

stops.name: Gore Canyon — the wild Colorado
stops.blurb: No road reaches here: whitewater a thousand feet below the window, canyon walls closing to the sky.

stops.name: Glenwood Springs — hot-springs stopover
stops.blurb: Step off for the night: the world's largest hot-springs pool steams under the mountains a walk from the platform.

stops.name: Dinner in the canyon dusk
stops.blurb: White tablecloths and canyon light — the dining car's best hour, or a grill on the springs terrace.

days.title: Ruby Canyon, the desert and the Sierra approach
days.summary: Ruby Canyon's red walls at dawn, Utah's painted desert all day, Salt Lake in the night, and the Nevada basin run to Reno.

stops.name: Ruby Canyon at dawn
stops.blurb: Red sandstone walls catch first light on the Utah line — river, rock and not a road in sight.

stops.name: Salt Lake City — the midnight call
stops.blurb: The Mormon capital glitters against the Wasatch as the train pauses in the small hours.

stops.name: Reno — the biggest little stopover
stops.blurb: Out of the desert night into Reno's neon — a stopover night before the Sierra day.

days.title: Donner Pass and down to the Bay
days.summary: The Sierra Nevada by morning — snowsheds and thousand-foot drops over Donner Lake — then gold country, Sacramento, and the Pacific shore into San Francisco Bay.

stops.name: Donner Pass — the Sierra crossing
stops.blurb: The train hangs on the mountain wall above Donner Lake — the hardest-won miles in American railroading.

stops.name: Sacramento — gold-rush capital
stops.blurb: Down through the gold country to the state capital and the great railway museum beside the tracks.

stops.name: San Francisco Bay — journey's end
stops.blurb: The rails end at the water: across the bay, the city on its hills — one continent, coast to coast, behind you.
